assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson’s hybrid achievement makes classical learning, lyric intensity, narrative experiment and visual form mutually transformative across an unusually distinctive body of work.
assessment.attribution: Credit Anne Carson alone for a multilingual-range poetic and essayistic oeuvre exemplified by Autobiography of Red and Nox.
assessment.maturity: The representative works indicate sustained formal reinvention rather than a single achievement.
uncertainties: Assessment of the full multilingual and cross-generic corpus is necessarily incomplete.
The relative force of visual and performative dimensions in translation is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cixous has persistently expanded the relations among autobiography, philosophy, fiction and drama, making language itself a site of intellectual and imaginative discovery.
assessment.attribution: Credit Hélène Cixous alone for the experimental French-language oeuvre represented by The Book of Promethea and The Third Body.
assessment.maturity: Its long multigenre continuity and formal risk support recognition of a mature, consequential contribution.
uncertainties: The balance between literary, theoretical and dramatic work requires broader corpus coverage.
English translations may not fully convey the linguistic texture of the French.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adonis’s sustained remaking of Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and dialogue with inherited forms constitutes a major modern lyric project.
assessment.attribution: Credit Adonis alone for the Arabic-language poetic and essayistic achievement, including Songs of Mihyar the Damascene.
assessment.maturity: The scale and durability of the poetic project make the case one of long-developed mastery.
uncertainties: Translation cannot settle the full linguistic achievement of Arabic prosody and diction.
Comparative assessment of the complete later oeuvre remains limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pynchon’s encyclopedic novels have enlarged the possibilities of fiction by joining systems of power, science, history and countercultural imagination in singularly complex forms.
assessment.attribution: Credit Thomas Pynchon alone for the novelistic oeuvre represented by Gravity’s Rainbow and Mason & Dixon.
assessment.maturity: The work demonstrates enduring formal ambition and a sustained ability to make vast historical materials narratively volatile.
uncertainties: The density and scale of the oeuvre make comprehensive comparative evaluation difficult.
The relation between maximalist invention and emotional range warrants continued assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Murnane’s radically inward fiction develops landscape, memory and mental imagery into an unmistakable imaginative system with exceptional formal coherence.
assessment.attribution: Credit Gerald Murnane alone for the English-language fiction represented by The Plains and Border Districts.
assessment.maturity: The persistent project appears highly resolved, with later work deepening rather than merely repeating its methods.
uncertainties: The deliberately narrow experiential and geographic compass may limit assessment of the oeuvre’s total range.
Full access to and comparison across the corpus is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cărtărescu’s densely patterned prose turns body, memory and dream into an expansive metaphysical architecture, combining visionary force with sustained narrative invention.
assessment.attribution: Credit Mircea Cărtărescu alone for the Romanian-language fictional and poetic project represented by Blinding and Solenoid.
assessment.maturity: The representative large-scale works suggest a fully developed and ambitious oeuvre.
uncertainties: Translations may mediate crucial rhythmic and lexical effects.
The standing of the poetic work alongside the fiction requires fuller corpus comparison.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright’s polyphonic narratives renew the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time, with Carpentaria demonstrating exceptional imaginative scale.
assessment.attribution: Credit Alexis Wright alone for the English-language fictional and nonfictional oeuvre represented by Carpentaria and The Swan Book.
assessment.maturity: The work shows sustained formal purpose and a developed capacity to make collective histories literary form.
uncertainties: A fuller assessment of the nonfiction and complete fiction is needed.
Reception through non-Indigenous critical frameworks may obscure features of oral and communal form.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Can Xue’s dreamlike fiction persistently unsettles psychology, space and causality, pursuing a rare and uncompromising imaginative logic.
assessment.attribution: Credit Can Xue alone for the Chinese-language fiction represented by Frontier and Love in the New Millennium.
assessment.maturity: The recurrence of this distinctive method across a substantial body of work supports its seriousness and durability.
uncertainties: Translation creates particular uncertainty about stylistic precision and tonal force.
The balance of innovation, accessibility and sustained development across the full oeuvre needs broader coverage.
